title: People Search & Telephone OSINT
description: Deep dive into people search engines, telephone number investigation, VoIP analysis, carrier lookup, and advanced phone OSINT techniques. Covers CLI tools, GUI tools, APIs, and manual techniques.

sections.title: What Are People Search Engines?
sections.description: People search engines aggregate publicly available information from multiple sources — public records, online directories, social media, websites — and present it in one place. Originally US-focused but now global.
topics: Aggregates data from public records, directories, social media
Use pivoting — one piece of info leads to another
Never click random advertisements on these sites
Document everything you find — data is data
Don't pay for information — focus on free techniques
Aggregation does not mean accuracy — always verify
sections.note: A search result is only a lead until you independently confirm it belongs to your target. Same name can belong to different people. Databases can be outdated.

sections.note: This works on some sites where data is loaded in the DOM but visually hidden with CSS. It does not bypass actual server-side paywalls.

sections.title: OSINT Pivoting Technique
sections.description: Pivoting is the core skill of people search OSINT. Take one piece of information and use it to discover additional related information. Chain multiple pivots to build a complete picture.
topics: Name → Phone number → Address → Relatives
Email → Username → Social profiles → Location
Phone → Carrier → VoIP provider → Linked accounts
Address → Property records → Owner name → Business records
Username → GitHub → Email in commits → Real name
Profile picture → Reverse image → Other platforms → Location metadata

sections.title: Telephone Number OSINT — Basics
sections.description: Phone number investigation starts with understanding what type of number you are dealing with. The number type determines what information is available and what investigative steps to take next.
topics: Step 1: Carrier identification — who provides this number?
Step 2: Number type — mobile, landline, or VoIP?
Step 3: Geographic region — country, area code, city
Step 4: Reverse lookup — who is associated with this number?
Step 5: Cross-reference — does this number appear elsewhere online?

sections.title: VoIP — Understanding the Technology
sections.description: VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) transmits voice as digital packets over the internet instead of traditional telephone networks. Understanding VoIP is critical for phone OSINT.
topics: Fixed VoIP — tied to a physical location (home/office). More traceable.
Non-fixed VoIP — not tied to a location. Easier to obtain anonymously.
Google Voice, Twilio, TextNow, Burner — common VoIP providers
SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) — manages call setup and termination
RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) — carries actual voice/video data
PSTN (Public Switched Telephone Network) — traditional phone infrastructure
VPN does NOT make VoIP untraceable — account records, payment info, device data still exist
sections.note: If carrier lookup shows Google Voice, Twilio, or similar — it is likely a VoIP number. This means the number may not be tied to a real physical location or identity.

sections.title: VoIP Number Investigation
sections.description: When a number is identified as VoIP, standard reverse lookup may not work. These techniques help investigate VoIP numbers specifically.
sections.note: VoIP numbers can be registered with fake names. Focus on behavioral patterns, linked accounts, and cross-platform correlation rather than just the number itself.
